identity.name: British Overseas Territories
alt_names: Overseas Territories of the United Kingdom

land.text: the dependencies the United Kingdom held as Crown colonies (until 1 January 1983) and British Dependent Territories (1983-2002)

predecessors.note: The territories were not new land: the Act of 2002 gave the existing dependent territories their present name.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape without the Falkland Islands and Gibraltar, which have their own dossiers: what remains is South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands and Bermuda; holds 2002-2023

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 20,560 km2 shape is 64 gazetteer cells: 44 in the Falkland Islands, 9 in South Georgia, 1 in Bermuda and 1 in Gibraltar, with 9 more cells strung between them. The page's total for the 13 territories outside Antarctica is 18,015 km2 (text) or 18,105 km2 (table), so the shape is within range (ratio 1.14) but covers only four of the 14 territories (Falklands 12,173, South Georgia and South Sandwich 3,903, Bermuda 54, Gibraltar 6.5 km2). The Falklands and Gibraltar already have colony dossiers (falkland-islands, gibraltar), so they are subtracted to avoid drawing them twice. The other ten territories, most of them under one grid cell, and the 1,709,400 km2 British Antarctic Territory are not in the shape. Years: the Act that named the Territories dates from 2002; the 2000-2001 cells are the same territories as British Dependent Territories.

correction.text: the Cliopatria shape without the Falkland Islands and Gibraltar, which have their own dossiers: what remains is South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands and Bermuda; 2024

keyframe_review.note: Same 20,560 km2 shape as 2000-2023. The British Indian Ocean Territory is not in it: on 3 October 2024 the UK and Mauritius announced an agreement under which the UK would cede sovereignty, finalised in May 2025 and pending ratification on the page, so no loss is recorded.

region.text: the overseas territories in Cliopatria's shape (here: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, and Bermuda; the Falklands and Gibraltar are drawn by their own dossiers)

ledger.note: 2002: the dependent territories become the British Overseas Territories. The page names the 'British Overseas Territories Act 2002' as the law that introduced the current name; earlier they were 'Crown colonies' (until 1 January 1983) and 'British Dependent Territories' (1983-2002). The page gives no month.

certainty.note: Island and coastline limits; sovereignty claims over the Falklands, South Georgia and Gibraltar do not move the drawn coast.

sources.title: British Overseas Territories
sources.note: Name and earlier names, the 14 territories and areas, administrative centres, the 2024 British Indian Ocean Territory sovereignty agreement. The only page opened (page budget 1-2).

notes:
British Overseas Territories, written by eu-22-g on 2026-11-01 from one page (the article).

This Cliopatria row is an aggregate of dependencies, not a state: typed colony (a dependency ruled from London, tinted as the United Kingdom's) and begun in 2002, when the page says the Territories took their present name, not in 2000 where Cliopatria starts its shape. The shape duplicates the falkland-islands and gibraltar dossiers (both colonies already written) and omits ten of the 14 territories (Akrotiri and Dhekelia 255 km2, Anguilla 91, British Indian Ocean Territory 60, British Virgin Islands 153, Cayman Islands 264, Montserrat 101, Pitcairn 47, Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha 420, Turks and Caicos 948, British Antarctic Territory 1,709,400). The verdict subtracts the two that have dossiers. The remaining parts, Bermuda and South Georgia with the South Sandwich Islands, have no dossier of their own: counterparts_needing_dossiers in the report.

No capital is given: the page lists an administrative centre per territory (Hamilton for Bermuda, King Edward Point for South Georgia) and the Territories are ruled from London. The British Indian Ocean Territory agreement of 3 October 2024 is a pending cession and is not recorded as a loss. The Falklands War (1982), the Gibraltar and Falklands disputes are in the falkland-islands and gibraltar dossiers.
